newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary repo cuts seen leading to lower yields.
newsitem.headline: Hungary repo cuts seen leading to lower yields.

text.p: Weekend repo rate cuts by Hungary's central bank (NBH) have opened the way to further drops in government security yields, but will not have a substantial impact until the NBH cuts its longer-term deposit rates, traders said on Monday.
"The NBH admitted that it expects a moderate drop in yields, and this will happen," said Tamas Puskas of Raiffeisen Securities.

The NBH reduced the overnight repo rate to 26.75 percent from 27 percent on Saturday, the one-week repo rate to 26.75 percent from 27 percent, while the overnight reverse repo rate was cut to 17.25 percent from 17.50 percent.

Traders said one and three-month Treasury bill yields dropped five to 10 basis points on the secondary market on Monday following the repo cuts, while the yields on one-year and longer maturities eased by some five points.
They added that six- and twelve month-discount Treasury bills are unlikely to drop much due to the repo cuts.
"These maturities will not change much as the NBH did not cut its six- and twelve month deposit rate," said Gabor Szogi of Creditanstalt.

Traders do not expect substantial change in yields this week as the market is quiet ahead of four days of holidays starting on Thursday, they said, adding that demand for longer than one-year government securities was likely to rise in the near future.

Zsolt Bango of Gog Securities said he saw a decrease of a maximum 10 to 30 basis points in yields on shorter term papers over the next one month, while two- and three-year government bonds could drop by 30 to 50 points.
Puskas said the NBH may cut its six-month and 12-month deposit rates in the next few weeks and this would weigh on longer-term yields.
"As soon as the (NBH) depo rates are lowered, the stress on the (government bond) market will shift to the demand side from the supply," he said.
